text: I couldn't review this previously because it just wouldn't run correctly on either of my PCs. I had hoped it'd be a good travel game on my laptop, but didn't work. However, it works great on the Steam Frame, and I've really been enjoying it. Sort of gives me Dave the Diver timed vibes, but with some pretty plot specific cop stuff.

An absolute side-scrolling blast. And, just like the old side-scrollers this was inspired by, you'll probably need multiple retries just to complete the game. But that just means I get to enjoy the gorgeous pixel art and wonderful sound design for longer!
No skillbased matchmaking, they ban accounts for like 1 day when they use obvious cheats, and they're constantly shilling microtransactions for cosmetics for a game I purchased.

They really nailed the noir with talking animals style, it's worth recommending on that alone. A cool creative thing done well.

In fact, since the style was more or less perfect, I sort of... found myself not liking the writing as much as I expected to - because the style already set up a very high expectations bar. Again, though, it's fine, and it was great to see a unique game like that.

This is a great game with a unique, jack-of-all-trade gameplay mix of combat, diving, fishing, farming and business/resource management. Story's great too, with lots of post-endgame stuff to do: side-missions, collectables, and stuff. 

One warning though: it will either induce a midlife crisis that will make you want to leave your current job and life behind to look for jobs on beachside restaurants on a paradisiacal island or it will induce expensive sushi/seafood cravings... or both. Play it at your own risk.

I enjoyed. Although a little tedious at times I thought the overall vibe, story, and gameplay was spooky and compelling enough to keep me coming back. I did get the bad ending but I do seem to have a great way of doing that in the silent hill games. 😌

I've always been a sucker for Japanese culture and all things horror related so picking up this game was a no brainer. The storyline was excellent. It was hard to stop and put down the controller every time I would play. Hinako's story had me sucked in and I was rooting for her the entire time. The aesthetic is also very beautiful in my opinion. Even though the enemies are supposed to be horrifying and grotesque, there was a beauty to each of them.

Absolute game of the year. My only complaint is the really odd movement noises being played in the library cutscenes. It just didn't match up with the movement of the characters and it sounded like it was coming from somewhere outside of the game.

I saw the trailer on YouTube and thought it looked really cool. I was disappointed to find out it was just a short little student project and not a full game. The game looks pretty good and the combat took a bit to get used to. Not in a bad way and once I got the hang of it I think it feels good. If it was a full game I’d love to see what kind of other moves you could get. I really like the idea of healing by stealing the melting wax of the enemies. No UI, the health is how tall the candle is. It ended right as I was really getting into it. 

I tried 3 or 4 times to get the beat under 10 minutes achievement and kept being a tiny bit too slow. I turned on God Mode and it still worked so you can cheat to get it if you want.

Fun story, isn't as open as you may think it is at the start, all the weapons and armor are 1 time use and some aren't used at all. When defeating bosses, combat is a bit repetitive (some magic would have been cool) but there isn't much you can do with this concept. Good Game.

The other 25% of the game for me was dealing with the weird alien/other AI somehow seeing me through walls or behind chairs and honestly it became quite the chore to deal with. A fantastic game, because it's the good old Half-Life, just with a fresh coat of paint. Pretty much everything is excellent, except for one thing: Xen. The world of mushrooms and ugly aliens unfortunately overstays its welcome and feels overdesigned. Despite that, the game works brilliantly as a whole. Highly recommended.

Huge W to the Thompson brothers! 

After hearing all praise surrounding their newest title, "Well Dweller", I decided to take a look into their catologue of games and play through all of them from oldest to newest. Sheepo was the first game of theirs I had completed and really gave me a tatse for the quality of the games they create. As of writing this review I have just 100% completed "Islets", and can't wait to continue with "Crypt Custodian!" Obviously this game does have sertain flaws to it especially when comparing it to Kyle and Eric's newer titles, but for their first game I was left very impressed with the creativity behind this title. Fun and sometimes challenging platforming, really viby music to accompany this game's soundtrack, and a super cute and gorgeous artstyle are all factors that have made me come to love Sheepo as a game. For sure would reccomend! ;)

Buy it only when its on sale. Really good game, has a good plot but as others have noted, the fights get repetitive. Takes about 7 hours to complete the entire campaign. Wished there was some sort of a minimap but its not like you can't enjoy the game without it. While I do like the how smooth the mechanics are when it comes to fights and moving around, it does get to a point where you'd wish there was more. Very close to a walking simulator with seemingly repetitive fights.

I don't recommend this game simply because it is not my style of game. It is a passive "loot-em-up" where the main point is completionism. Fill up the encyclopedia, unlock all the upgrades, check all the boxes, check check check. It is very light on story and actual gameplay. 

I understand many people are into that type of game. And if you are, you will love this one. The graphics/art style are great, the music is great, the game is extremely polished. 

But it is not the game for me. I need something more gripping, whether it's story or gameplay, and this one lacks both.

One of the most important indie games of all time. The story, while mainly subversive, is painful, impactful, and critical in a world where few game developers are willing to broach such intense topics. Grief is the surface tension of a much deeper and important narrative within Gris, so I encourage you to look into the symbols and atmosphere of the game to find what lies behind this platformer.
